a king of the solar dynasty, powerful, named Brahmadatta. / By that king, great austerity was performed for a long time, O ruler of the gods.

The practice of the five fires was performed by him repeatedly, / and austerities such as fasts lasting a month were undertaken many times.

6.130.m:
Thus for a very long time, great austerity was performed by the king. / Then I appeared before him to grant a boon, O woman of excellent complexion:

'Brahmadatta, listen to my great word, O king: / whatever you desire always, that I grant; there is no doubt.'

By him it was said: 'O Lord of gods, if what is desired is to be given, / let only one boon be granted to me forever, O God:

by my name indeed, O Lord of gods, let there be an īśvara on earth.' / Pleased by that speech, a boon was granted by me, O sinless one:

'Then I indeed dwell with you, O ruler of the gods. / Remaining here, fasting, one who performs complete devotion,

I grant his desired wishes for as long as the fourteen Indras [endure]. / And those Brahmins who come here and perform the recitation of the Rudra hymns and other prayers,

who especially perform them—listen to what I give to them: / happiness with a wife, happiness with a son, and that which causes wealth to increase,

fame, sovereignty, and likewise the destruction of diseases and the like. / All that is quickly attained as desired, even in the Kali yuga.

In this terrible Kali yuga, my devotees on earth, O Pārvatī, / having come here, having consecrated [an image], and having stayed for five days—

I grant them their desired objects; truly, truly, O ruler of the gods!' / Having established [the liṅga] named Brahmadatta, and a second named Brahmacārin,

6.130.m:
[and] having established Gaṅgādhara, and having resided there for five days, / that king then went back to his own kingdom.

Brahmadatta, renowned in the world as exceedingly great, / knowing dharma, ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years.

Then, after some time, having enjoyed the kingdom, that king / went to the world of Śiva, the supreme abode known as Brahman.

Two gods abide there indicating my names: / one is known as Brahmacārīśa, the other as Gaṅgādhara.

Those people who perform worship especially in my place, / to them I give everything desired here; of this there is no doubt.

The place itself is the liṅga; it should always be visited by men. / There flowers, incense, and various offerings of food,

whichever wise man offers, he surely attains everything. / With bilva leaves, flowers, or with sandalwood and the like,

they worship in my place; to them I grant everything. / Whoever constantly listens to this Brahmacārin narrative,

having obtained happiness in this world, goes to the presence of Śiva, / where the god Gaṅgādhara, the bestower of prosperity, constantly remains.

6.130.m:
The second, named Brahmacārīśa, is always present. / Through the union of meditation on the two, one surely attains Śivahood.

From seeing [them], disease is destroyed; from worship, one attains long life; / and from bathing there, O ruler of the gods, one shares in liberation; of this there is no doubt.

Listen, O beautiful woman, I shall declare a most wonderful tīrtha / renowned as Rājakhaṅga, situated particularly on the Sābharmatī.

Born in the solar dynasty was a king named Kartana, / of evil conduct, sinful, and a reviler of Brahmins,

treacherous to his guru, ever angry, a scorner of all rites, / constantly devoted to others' wives, and constantly reviling Viṣṇu,

he constantly oppressed the subjects in many ways. / Such a wicked soul always lived on the earth.

When some time had passed in this manner, listen truthfully, O beautiful woman: / through sin and through the turn of fate, leprosy arose [in him].

Gazing upon his own body and reflecting again and again, / wondering 'What should be done?', he became filled with anxiety.

Once, by the turn of fate, he went into the forest to amuse himself; / reaching the bank of the Sābharmatī there, he remained.

6.130.m:
Bathing was performed by him there, and the excellent water was drunk. / Instantly through bathing there, his body became celestial,

seen as a beautiful golden form, O daughter of the mountain! / At that very moment, that king was transformed; of this there is no doubt.

Having obtained a divine form, the king then, for some time, / having enjoyed the kingdom, O ruler of the gods, went to the supreme abode.

Then this tīrtha became known by the name Rājakhaṅga. / Those who perform ablutions here, or whoever makes a gift,

having enjoyed happiness in this world, goes to Viṣṇu's eternal [abode]. / There is no disease for them, nor sorrow at any time.

A man who daily bathes in this pool known as the royal pool / attains heaven and is honored by Brahmā and others.

In the Kṛta age, it was named Satyeśvara; in the Tretā age, Bhuvaneśvara; / it was renowned as Rājeśvara in the Dvāpara age, O daughter of the mountain.

In this terrible Kali yuga, it became hidden, and the sovereign of the universe [is concealed]; / hence the sacred tīrtha came to be named Rājakhaṅga.

Those who offer libations with faith to the ancestors here, / those men are praised as performers of meritorious deeds on earth.

Even slayers of Brahmins and slayers of children who bathe here / are freed from those sins and go to the presence of Śiva.

And those men who perform the release of a dark bull into the Sābhramatī, / their ancestors indeed remain satisfied until the universal dissolution.

This divine narrative named Rājakhaṅga, / those men who hear it, O Goddess, have no fear.

Diseases and blemishes are destroyed by hearing and reciting it.

Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-fifth chapter, entitled "The Glorification of the Sābharmatī," in the dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara, in the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Padma Purāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand verses.

The one hundred and thirty-sixth chapter. Pārvatī said: / The Sābharmatī, emerging from the Nandikuṇḍa, through which lands [did it flow]?

purify as she flowed? Tell me which regions [they were], / and which sacred places she made after crossing Mount Arbuda.

Sūta said: / When this was spoken there by the goddess, Mahādeva, the sovereign of the universe, / spoke words to Pārvatī, who enchants the universe.

Mahādeva said: / First from Nandikuṇḍa, the supremely purifying sacred place, / the sacred place Kapālamocana was proclaimed by the sages.

It is a sacred place surpassing all in splendor, supreme purifier among purifiers; / here the skull known as Brahmā's was cast off by me.

Therefore, O Pārvatī, the sacred place became known as Kapālamocana, / purifying all beings, manifest, renowned in the world.

That sacred place, a king of sacred places, is known as Kapālakuṇḍa, / where gods as well as Nāgas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, and others

magnanimous beings dwell in that spotless, auspicious sacred place, / celebrated in the three worlds, granting gifts and bestowing liberation.

Having bathed there and become pure, one should worship the Lord of the Skull; / having fasted for one night, and having fed Brahmins,

even by the gift of cloth there one obtains the fruit of an Agnihotra sacrifice. / But whatever person who, undertaking the vow of seeing [the shrine] at that sacred place,

casts off his body and self, surely goes to the world of Śiva. / Formerly, by bathing in this sacred place, Saudāsa was freed from the killing of a Brahmin

and attained pure knowledge, O Queen of the gods. / Born in the lineage of Bhagīratha was the mighty Sudāsa;

his son was Mitrasaha, renowned as Saudāsa. / Due to Vasiṣṭha's curse, Saudāsa attained a demonic body;

Thus ends the Vikīrṇa Ford. / Beyond this ford is an unequaled ford born of Śvetā, / where the Śvetā River was born from the ashes of my back and belly.

renowned in the three worlds, destroying all sins, / born from contact with the ash of Hara's limbs and honored by the gods.

A man who bathes in it, pure and restrained, having dwelt [there] for three nights / and beholding Mahākāleśvara, is glorified in the world of Rudra.

He who offers a rice-ball to the ancestors with kuśa grass and sesame seeds upon its bank, / his ancestors become fully satisfied; of this there is no doubt.

Śvetagaṅgā is exceedingly meritorious, releasing from suffering and poverty; / by bathing there, O Goddess, supreme happiness is attained.

At its holy confluence, O Pārvatī, I always dwell; / those who make gifts here and bathe there, O beautiful one,

infinite fruit shall be theirs; of this there is indeed no doubt. / There the god Bhūteśvara surely dwells at the confluence.

Those best of men who offer incense, lamps, flowers, and the light-waving ceremony there, / those men are embodiments of merit.

He who takes a bilva leaf and offers it atop Śiva, / always obtains his desire in the Śvetā in the presence of Śiva.

6.131.m: Mahādeva said: / Then, intent on the pilgrimage to sacred places, one should go to Gaṇatīrtha, / proclaimed as Triviṣṭapa by the gaṇas on the bank of the Candanā.
A man having bathed with composure at Triviṣṭapa on the full-moon day— / no doubt should be entertained here—is liberated from the killing of a Brahmin.
He whose stay at Triviṣṭapa lasts for the four rainy months, / he too is meritorious, O noble goddess, and is honored in the realm of Rudra.
A man having bathed at Gaṇatīrtha while fasting on the dark eighth day, / having bathed at the confluence with the Bakulā, goes to heaven.
A man having bathed at that tīrtha and having beheld Bakuleśa, / by the grace of Gaṇeśvara shall attain the status of a gaṇa.
This supreme, purifying [narrative] increases merit and longevity; / hearing it, a man indeed obtains merit equal to bathing in the Gaṅgā.
Staying here without food, self-controlled and focused, / he who thus chants to the supreme god, the charming Lord of Gaṇas,
attains all enjoyments—truly, truly, O fair-faced goddess. / Here the heroic king Viśvadatta, born of the lunar dynasty,
performed great austerities for a long time, O ruler of gods; / he then attained the status of a gaṇa through the grace of the glorious Gaṇeśa.
Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Hoḍa, Kauśītaka the sage, / Bharadvāja, Aṅgiras, Viśvāmitra, and Vāmana—
all these sages indeed, of meritorious form, O supreme goddess, / constantly render service through the grace of the glorious Gaṇeśa.
The childless obtains sons; the penniless obtains wealth; / the unlearned obtains learning; one seeking liberation attains liberation.
What need is there to say more, again and again, O fair-faced goddess? / Whoever performs a bath here, or performs worship,
is freed from all sins and goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / Between Śiva in the form of Viṣṇu and Viṣṇu in the form of Śiva,
I see no difference, O goddess, and through the grace of the glorious Viṣṇu [this is so].

6.139.m:
Mahādeva said:
On the northern bank of the Sābhramatī there is the renowned Agnitīrtha; / to the northeast of it, not very far away, is situated
the tīrtha named Pāleśvara, where Caṇḍī is installed; / that is a seat of the Mothers of Yoga, which bestows all accomplishments,
where those Mothers reside for the sake of all the gods, / having undertaken supreme effort for the sake of favoring the worlds.
Having stayed three nights at that tīrtha, firm in his vow, / one should approach that lord, Caṇḍikeśvara, the ruler of gods.
Having bathed in the Sābhramatī in the vicinity of Mātṛtīrtha, / engaged in the proper rule of absorption, one should indeed go to the circle of the Mothers.
A person attains the fruit of giving a thousand cows. / A man having bathed at Agnitīrtha, when sight of Cāmuṇḍā has been made,
no fear arises for him born of rākṣasas, bhūtas, or piśācas. / Where the river Gokhurā joins with the Sābhramatī,
thousands of tīrthas abide there, O ruler of gods. / A śrāddha should be performed there with sesame powder, O Pārvatī;
having offered rice-balls and fed the twice-born, one reaches the imperishable realm. / Where King Kukardama, most sinful, uncontrollable, and wicked,
foolish, filled with arrogance, a reviler of the twice-born, / a slayer of cows, a killer of the strong, most sinful and ever intractable,
was ruling in the city called Piṇḍāra— / then death arrived in the course of righteousness, O ruler of gods.
Having died, he was born there in the form of a preta, O great goddess, / yellow-faced, with a shriveled mouth, yellow hair, and rough,
very tall, hairy, tormented by hunger and thirst, / subsisting on air, wandering here and there,
accompanied by many pretas, weeping piteously, crying "Alas! Alas!" / "What should be done?" said those pretas who were near him;
they too were then weeping, afflicted by hunger, thirst, and the like. / Other pretas of wicked soul joined the king's company.
Along with the king they wander through many deserted lands; / neither water nor food is ever seen along the road.
Those pretas of terrible appearance roam upon the surface of the earth; / they eat corpse flesh and continually drink blood.
Thus King Kukardama, ever surrounded by them, / once by the workings of fate came upon the hermitage of his guru.

There was merit done in a former birth; by that connection he came [there]. / Pārvatī said:
What merit indeed was done by him? Tell me, O Lord, Master of the Universe!
This sinful and wicked soul who brought distress to brāhmaṇas— / how did the company of the virtuous happen for him? Tell me that, which is difficult to comprehend.

Mahādeva said:
What was done in a former birth by this lord of men, / I shall relate all that to you; listen, O daughter of the mountain.
In a former birth, O goddess, he was a brāhmaṇa, a reciter of the Vedas; / having worshipped Mahādeva and performed the worship of guests,
that best of brāhmaṇas would eat his daily meal. / By the power of that merit, in the city called Piḍāra,
he was born as a king known as Kukardama. / In deed and in thought, no merit whatsoever was done by him [as king];
by that divine ordinance, having died, he became a king of pretas, / dry-faced, of shriveled form, yellow in color, terrifying.
Merit acquired in a previous birth does not perish, O ruler of gods; / through the connection of that merit, he came to his guru's hermitage.
Kahoḍa resided there; by him the king of pretas was then seen, / dry-faced, of shriveled form, yellow in color, terrifying,
deep-eyed, a great sinner, accompanied by evil pretas, / with erect hair, matted locks, appearing like Death, dreadful.

Having seen him thus, O goddess, the brāhmaṇa became agitated. / Kahoḍa said:
In this charming, truly exceedingly wonderful place,
at the tīrtha of Agnipāleśvara, I continually dwell, O king. / You were our patron of sacrifice; how have you become a king of pretas,
evil-minded, of wicked form, resembling Death, and terrifying? / By the fruition of what deed were you born [thus] on the auspicious surface of the earth?

The preta said:
Listen, O brāhmaṇa, to my sin that was committed in my previous birth: / I was King Kukardama in the city named Piṇḍāra.
While residing there, O lord, hear what was indeed done by me: / the harming of brāhmaṇas, and formerly the speaking of untruths and the like;
the oppression of subjects, and constant injury to living beings; / I was an inflictor of suffering upon cows, a breaker of the vows of brāhmaṇas,
always unbathed, O vipra, a reviler of virtuous people, / constantly intent on slandering Viṣṇu, and a reviler of Vaiṣṇavas,
ill-behaved and wicked-souled, ever consorting with a Śūdra woman; / eating here and there without care, never devoted to purification.
By the conjunction of that karma, having died, O king among the twice-born, / I fell into the womb of a preta and became miserable in many ways.
For him who has neither mother nor father, nor kinfolk and relatives, / the guru is his relative, the guru is his mother, and the guru is indeed his father.
Knowing this, O brāhmaṇa, you ought to grant liberation.

Kahoḍa said:
Listen, O best of kings, I shall carry out your request: / you shall indeed attain liberation immediately here, there is no doubt.
And the pretas led by eleven who are associated with you, / they too shall attain liberation, especially at this excellent tīrtha.
Then, having gone to the sacred bathing place with that brāhmaṇa, O goddess of gods, / he had the rites of sesame, funeral cakes, and water performed by all.

There is no restriction of month nor lunar day, O goddess, having gone to the sacred bathing place again and again; / the ancestral offering and other rites should be performed: this was declared to me by Brahmā in ancient times.
When the rite was performed, O sovereign of the gods, they were freed at that king of sacred bathing places; / mounted on excellent celestial chariots, they went to my own city.
Where the Gokhurā joins with the Sābhramatī, O goddess of gods, / bathing and giving there yields the fruit of ten million sacrifices.
Where Agnitīrtha is situated, known as Kapāleśvara, / liberation is proclaimed there; truly, truly, it shall surely be so.
